# atomvm-cbor 0.2.0

This is the first Hex.pm release of `atomvm_cbor`, providing the OTP application `avm_cbor`. Public Git tag `v0.1.1` is the reproducible source and benchmark baseline and was never published to Hex.pm.

## What is new

- Partial/deferred decoding through `partial_decode/1,2`, `partial_deep_decode/1`, and opaque descriptor accessors.
- Deterministic encoding and strict deterministic input validation, including definite-length enforcement, preferred-width checks, duplicate-map-key rejection, and ordering by original encoded key bytes.
- Preferred serialization support without changing the default non-preferred behavior.
- Bounded full and partial decode with depth, node, total-input, per-string, cumulative-string, and partial-string limits.
- Structured malformed/truncated-input errors across full, sequence, and partial paths.
- One-pass option normalization into fixed internal state, avoiding repeated proplist allocation and lookup in recursive loops.
- Existing public `{text, Binary}`, `{map, Pairs}`, and `{tag, Number, Value}` representations remain supported.

## Host performance

Measurements compare exact public `v0.1.1` with the audited 0.2.0 implementation on the same Dell host and harness: OTP 27, five complete paired runs, with 31 samples after 1,000 warmups per run. Values are medians of the five run-level median/p95 nanoseconds per call; lower is better. Exact-head CI independently selects the unique greatest reachable SemVer below `VERSION` and enforces the unchanged +5% regression gate under OTP 29; missing or ambiguous baselines fail closed.

| Workload | v0.1.1 median/p95 ns | 0.2.0 median/p95 ns | Change (median/p95) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| malformed declared array | 1921 / 1941 | 476 / 484 | 75.22% / 75.06% faster |
| 32-item sequence decode | 5911 / 5971 | 4062 / 4157 | 31.28% / 30.38% faster |
| nested encode | 8204 / 8261 | 5832 / 5864 | 28.91% / 29.02% faster |
| nested decode | 2786 / 2826 | 2466 / 2516 | 11.49% / 10.97% faster |
| 64-byte string encode | 1975 / 1987 | 752 / 805 | 61.92% / 59.49% faster |
| 64-byte string decode | 2022 / 2056 | 1103 / 1119 | 45.45% / 45.57% faster |
| scalar encode | 1399 / 1415 | 147 / 153 | 89.49% / 89.19% faster |
| scalar decode | 1285 / 1305 | 309 / 317 | 75.95% / 75.71% faster |
| partial nested decode | N/A | 3181 / 3227 | N/A |
| deterministic map encode | N/A | 8484 / 8534 | N/A |
| deterministic map decode | N/A | 4652 / 4684 | N/A |

## Attached-device performance

The device measurements use the same CBOR payload and AtomVM 0.6.6 benchmark harness, with 50 iterations for common/partial work and 250 iterations for descriptor accessors after warmup. ESP32-S3 and RP2040 values are medians of five paired runs. WaveShare values are per-call averages from the matched v0.1.1 and exact final-code captures. They provide measured context, not a universal latency guarantee.

| Function | ESP32-S3 v0.1.1 µs | ESP32-S3 0.2.0 µs | Change | RP2040 v0.1.1 µs | RP2040 0.2.0 µs | Change | WaveShare N32R16V v0.1.1 µs | WaveShare N32R16V 0.2.0 µs | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `encode/1` | 8705.82 | 7120.54 | 18.21% faster | 7248.56 | 5118.92 | 29.38% faster | 6080.32 | 4064.56 | 33.15% faster |
| `decode/1` | 8508.98 | 8683.68 | 2.05% slower | 7105.50 | 6400.78 | 9.92% faster | 5853.32 | 4600.30 | 21.41% faster |
| `partial_decode/1` | N/A | 13109.00 | N/A | N/A | 9875.48 | N/A | N/A | 7518.24 | N/A |
| `partial_decode/2` | N/A | 13326.80 | N/A | N/A | 9928.18 | N/A | N/A | 7570.60 | N/A |
| `partial_deep_decode/1` | N/A | 10805.88 | N/A | N/A | 8243.96 | N/A | N/A | 5911.32 | N/A |
| `partial_value_bytes/1` | N/A | 767.53 | N/A | N/A | 579.66 | N/A | N/A | 562.63 | N/A |
| `partial_contents/1` | N/A | 959.06 | N/A | N/A | 506.69 | N/A | N/A | 607.53 | N/A |
| `partial_skip/1` | N/A | 380.07 | N/A | N/A | 228.66 | N/A | N/A | 295.30 | N/A |
| `partial_type/1` | N/A | 382.08 | N/A | N/A | 229.65 | N/A | N/A | 295.48 | N/A |
| `partial_count/1` | N/A | 381.27 | N/A | N/A | 229.65 | N/A | N/A | 296.33 | N/A |
| `partial_tag/1` | N/A | 438.55 | N/A | N/A | 253.83 | N/A | N/A | 360.91 | N/A |
| `partial_size/1` | N/A | 455.71 | N/A | N/A | 260.95 | N/A | N/A | 382.75 | N/A |

The WaveShare ESP32-S3-DEV-KIT-N32R16V (32 MB flash, 16 MB PSRAM) completed the exact-candidate maximum, benchmark, and 40-round retained-growth suites without a watchdog, backtrace, panic, abort, or out-of-memory marker. Its matched v0.1.1 benchmark capture is retained in the operator evidence directory. Earlier ESP32-S3 and RP2040 measurements remain useful constrained-target context, but those targets cannot materialize the 1 MiB harness input. Deployments on them must enforce a lower transport-ingress ceiling before buffering. Early and late heap/memory maxima were flat in the measured soak. This is bounded test evidence, not a claim that the software is leak-free or fully secure. See the [full validation report](../../docs/benchmarks/0.2.0.md).

## Compatibility and packaging

- Erlang/OTP 25 and later.
- AtomVM 0.6.6 validated.
- No runtime dependencies.
- Hex package: `atomvm_cbor`; OTP application: `avm_cbor`.
- HexDocs includes the overview, API guide, changelog, and license.

Rebar3:

```erlang
{deps, [
    {avm_cbor, "~> 0.2.0", {pkg, atomvm_cbor}}
]}.
```

Mix:

```elixir
{:avm_cbor, "~> 0.2.0", hex: :atomvm_cbor}
```

See the public benchmark runner and test suites in the repository to reproduce validation on your own systems.
